title: Biden’s Cabinet Picks, Part 2: Antony Blinken

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报 DealBook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的领袖，包括 J·D·

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在 NYTimes.com 上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并获得一个月的免费权限，畅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家准时收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today, I'm pleased to announce nominations and staff for critical foreign policy and national security positions in my administration.
sentences.zh: 今天，我很高兴宣布我的政府中关键外交政策和国家安全职位的提名人和工作人员。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 就在今天。

sentences.en: It's a team that reflects the fact that America is back, ready to lead the world, not retreat from it.
sentences.zh: 这是一个体现美国已经回归、准备领导世界而非从世界退缩这一事实的团队。

sentences.en: Part two of our look at the cabinet of President-elect Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 我们对当选总统乔·拜登内阁观察的第二部分。

sentences.en: As Secretary of State, I nominate Tony Blinken.
sentences.zh: 作为国务卿，我提名托尼·布林肯。

sentences.en: David Sanger on Biden's nominee for Secretary of State.
sentences.zh: 大卫·桑格谈拜登的国务卿提名人。

sentences.en: I've seen him in action.
sentences.zh: 我见过他雷厉风行的工作作风。

sentences.en: Tony is ready on day one.
sentences.zh: 托尼从上任第一天起就已准备就绪。

sentences.en: And what kind of foreign policy is possible after four years of American isolationism?
sentences.zh: 经历了四年的美国孤立主义之后，还可能实现什么样的外交政策？

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, December 2nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月2日，星期三。

sentences.en: David, I want to start by asking you the same question I asked our colleague Gina Smiley about Joe Biden's selection of his Treasury Secretary.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我想先问你一个问题，和之前我问我们同事吉娜·斯麦里关于乔·拜登挑选财政部长的问题一样。

sentences.en: And of course, we're going to be talking about his choice of Secretary of State.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们要谈的是他选择的国务卿。

sentences.en: How important is the role of the Secretary of State going to be, do you think, in this incoming administration?
sentences.zh: 你认为在即将上任的政府中，国务卿的角色会有多重要？

sentences.en: Well, historically and constitutionally, Michael, Secretary of State's always been
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，从历史和宪法角度来看，国务卿一直都是

sentences.en: the most important cabinet post after the president and the vice president and the first cabinet member who's in line for the presidency.
sentences.zh: 继总统和副总统之后最重要的内阁职位，也是总统继承顺位中的第一位内阁成员。

sentences.en: But it's particularly critical right now because Joe Biden is going to be consumed in his first six months by COVID-19, by domestic imperatives, and yet the world's given us
sentences.zh: 但它现在尤为关键，因为乔·拜登在上任的前六个月里将把精力耗费在新冠疫情和国内要务上，而世界却认为我们

sentences.en: up for dead.
sentences.zh: 已经不行了。

sentences.en: And so the Secretary of State is going to have to show that America is back, that America cares about allies, and that America is ready to lead.
sentences.zh: 因此，国务卿必须证明美国已经归来，美国关心盟友，并且美国已经准备好领导世界。

sentences.en: And the Secretary of State is the chief spokesperson for the president around the world.
sentences.zh: 而且国务卿是总统在世界各地的首席发言人。

sentences.en: And of course, has to be somebody who the rest of the world thinks really is in sync with the president.
sentences.zh: 当然，这个人必须让世界其他地方觉得他真的与总统同频共振。

sentences.en: Somebody who the rest of the world believes literally speaks word for word for the president.
sentences.zh: 一个让世界其他地方相信他可以一字不差地代表总统说话的人。

sentences.en: The most powerful secretaries of state in recent times have been those who no one doubted, had a relationship with the president that was so
sentences.zh: 近年来最有权势的国务卿都是那些没有人怀疑他们与总统的关系是如此

sentences.en: close that when the secretary spoke, it was like the president speaking.
sentences.zh: 亲密，以至于当国务卿说话时，就如同总统在说话一样。

sentences.en: And Joe Biden has picked in Tony Blinken, somebody who has been with him for 20 years, who can finish his sentences, who Biden once said could do any job in his administration.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登挑选的托尼·布林肯，是一个跟随了他20年、能接上他的话、拜登曾说他能胜任政府中任何工作的人。

sentences.en: And they will know that when
sentences.zh: 他们会知道，当

sentences.en: Blinken speaks, they might as well be listening to Biden.
sentences.zh: 布林肯说话时，就等同于在听拜登说话。

sentences.en: So I want to get to this extremely close relationship between Biden and Blinken, but I want to start with the backstory of Tony Blinken.
sentences.zh: 所以我想谈谈拜登和布林肯之间这种极其密切的关系，但我想从托尼·布林肯的背景故事开始。

sentences.en: He's not a household name like the secretaries of state that you just mentioned.
sentences.zh: 他不像你刚才提到的那些国务卿那样是个家喻户晓的名字。

sentences.en: And I wonder where his story starts.
sentences.zh: 我想知道他的故事是从哪里开始的。

sentences.en: Mr. President-elect, Vice President-elect Harris, thank you for your trust and your confidence.
sentences.zh: 当选总统先生、当选副总统哈里斯，感谢你们的信任与信心。

sentences.en: He's not a household name, though he's known well in Washington in foreign policy circles, but he's got this very rich backstory.
sentences.zh: 他并非家喻户晓，尽管他在华盛顿的外交政策圈里广为人知，但他有着非常丰富的背景故事。

sentences.en: For my family, as for so many generations of Americans, America has literally been the last best hope on earth.
sentences.zh: 对我的家庭而言，正如对无数代美国人一样，美国一直是地球上最后的最好希望。

sentences.en: And actually, Blinken told a little bit of the story when President-elect Biden formally announced his nomination as secretary of state.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当当选总统拜登正式宣布提名他为国务卿时，布林肯讲述了部分故事。

sentences.en: My grandfather, Maurice Blinken, fled pogroms in Russia and made a new life in America.
sentences.zh: 我的祖父莫里斯·布林肯逃离了俄罗斯的迫害，并在美国开启了新生活。

sentences.en: His son, my father, Donald Blinken, served in the United States Air Force during World War II and then as a United States ambassador.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子、我的父亲唐纳德·布林肯在二战期间服役于美国空军，后来担任美国大使。

sentences.en: Born in New York, parents divorced when he was about eight years old, and he moved to Paris where his new stepfather is a very well-known lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他在纽约出生，父母在他大约八岁时离异，他随母亲搬到巴黎，他的新继父是一位非常知名的律师。

sentences.en: And my late stepfather, Samuel Pizarro.
sentences.zh: 也就是我已故的继父塞缪尔·皮萨尔。

sentences.en: But had been a survivor of concentration camps.
sentences.zh: 但他曾是集中营的幸存者。

sentences.en: He was one of 900 children in his school in Bialystok, Poland, but the only one to survive the Holocaust after four years in concentration camps.
sentences.zh: 他是波兰比亚韦斯托克学校里900名孩子中唯一的幸存者，在经历了四年的集中营生活后，成为了唯一在大屠杀中幸存的人。

sentences.en: He was a Jewish kid whose entire town had been swept up by the Nazis.
sentences.zh: 他是一个犹太孩子，整个小镇都被纳粹席卷。

sentences.en: At the end of the war, he made a break from a death march into the woods in Bavaria.
sentences.zh: 战争结束时，他从通往巴伐利亚树林的死亡行军中逃了出来。

sentences.en: From his hiding place, he heard a deep rumbling sound.
sentences.zh: 从藏身处，他听到了低沉的轰鸣声。

sentences.en: It was a tank, but instead of the Iron Cross, he saw painted on its side a five-pointed white star.
sentences.zh: 那是一辆坦克，但它侧面画的不是铁十字，而是一个五角白星。

sentences.en: He ran to the tank.
sentences.zh: 他朝坦克跑去。

sentences.en: The hatch opened.
sentences.zh: 舱门打开了。

sentences.en: An African-American GI looked down at him.
sentences.zh: 一个非裔美国大兵低头看着他。

sentences.en: He got down on his knees and said the only three words that he knew in English that his mother taught him before the war.
sentences.zh: 他双膝跪地，说出了他母亲在战前教给他的仅有的三个英语单词。

sentences.en: God bless America.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑美国。

sentences.en: And it's really an amazing Holocaust survival story.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个惊人的大屠杀幸存故事。

sentences.en: But he told Blinken the stories of his survival from the camps.
sentences.zh: 但他把自己在集中营幸存的故事讲给了布林肯听。

sentences.en: And it deeply affected the way Blinken viewed the world.
sentences.zh: 这深刻地影响了布林肯看待世界的方式。

sentences.en: How so?
sentences.zh: 怎么说？

sentences.en: That's who we are.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们。

sentences.en: That's what America represents to the world, however imperfectly.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国向世界所代表的形象，尽管并不完美。

sentences.en: So what I think that story did for Blinken was cement his view that the United States has a singular role in the world.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为那个故事对布林肯的作用是巩固了他的看法，即美国在世界上扮演着独特角色。

sentences.en: Defending freedoms, defending human rights, a country that sometimes needs to intervene to guarantee the rights of others.
sentences.zh: 捍卫自由，捍卫人权，一个有时需要干预以保障他人权利的国家。

sentences.en: And that really keeps showing up after he launched his career in diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 这在他开启外交生涯后不断显现出来。

sentences.en: Well, tell me about that career.
sentences.zh: 那么跟我讲讲他的那段职业生涯吧。

sentences.en: Well, he left Paris, went to Harvard, dabbled in journalism and filmmaking for a while, but eventually decided that what he really wanted to do was be a diplomat.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他离开巴黎去了哈佛，做过一段时间的记者和电影制作，但最终决定他真正想做的是成为一名外交官。

sentences.en: He's fascinated by diplomacy, what makes the world tick, goes into the State Department young.
sentences.zh: 他对外交以及世界的运转规律充满着迷，很年轻就进入了国务院。

sentences.en: But his really formative period of time is ending up as a young staffer in Bill Clinton's National Security Council.
sentences.zh: 但他真正成型的时期是作为年轻幕僚进入比尔·克林顿的国家安全委员会。

sentences.en: And I think the story of Blinken's career has sort of been pushing up against that instinct that shows up so often in American history that the United States really should stay out of things more than get involved.
sentences.zh: 我认为布林肯职业生涯的故事某种程度上一直在对抗那种频繁出现在美国历史中的本能，即美国比起介入更应该置身事外。

sentences.en: And, you know, nowhere was that conflict clearer than in 1994.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这种冲突在1994年表现得最为清晰。

sentences.en: More than 100,000 are trying to escape Rwanda's capital, trying to escape this terrifying killing field.
sentences.zh: 超过十万人试图逃离卢旺达首都，试图逃离这片可怕的杀戮战场。

sentences.en: Tribal massacres continue in the Central African nation of Rwanda.
sentences.zh: 中非国家卢旺达的部族大屠杀仍在继续。

sentences.en: In one of the latest, hundreds of refugees were pulled out of a former UN compound and slaughtered by government troops with grenades, machine guns and machetes.
sentences.zh: 在最近的一次屠杀中，数百名难民被从一个前联合国营地拖出来，遭到政府军用手榴弹、机关枪和大砍刀残杀。

sentences.en: We're exposed to death every day and night.
sentences.zh: 我们日夜面临着死亡的威胁。

sentences.en: When Bill Clinton hesitated about sending American troops into Rwanda to stop a genocide.
sentences.zh: 当时比尔·克林顿在是否派遣美军进入卢旺达以制止种族灭绝一事上犹豫不决。

sentences.en: Our aims is to move food, medicine and other supplies to those in need as quickly as possible.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标是尽快将食品、药品和其他物资运送给需要的人。

sentences.en: And later on, Clinton said that that was the biggest regret of his presidency.
sentences.zh: 后来，克林顿表示那是他总统任期内最大的遗憾。

sentences.en: But I think it was also a very critical moment for Blinken because he recognized that while there's a significant cost when the United States gets overstretched,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这也是布林肯非常关键的时刻，因为他认识到，虽然当美国过度伸展时会付出沉重的代价，

sentences.en: what we used to call imperial overstretch, there's also a cost when the U.S.
sentences.zh: 也就是我们过去常说的帝国过度扩张，但当美国退缩导致人们死亡时，同样也要付出代价。

sentences.en: pulls back and people die.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In this case, hundreds of thousands of Tutsi Rwandans were murdered in a genocide.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，成千上万的图西族卢旺达人在种族灭绝中被谋杀。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: And there are many who came out of the Clinton administration thinking that with a relatively small showing of force, the United States might have saved those people,
sentences.zh: 许多从克林顿政府出来的人认为，只要动用相对较小的武力，美国本可以拯救那些人，

sentences.en: although that would have been an action that wasn't a vital American national intereSt.
sentences.zh: 尽管那可能不是一项生死攸关的美国国家利益行动。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Instead, it is a humanitarian intereSt.
sentences.zh: 相反，这是一项人道主义利益。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But it sounds like as the stepchild of a Holocaust survivor, Blinken leads unmistakably toward intervention in a case like that.
sentences.zh: 但听起来，作为大屠杀幸存者的继子，布林肯在那种情况下无疑倾向于军事干预。

sentences.en: I'd say that Blinken shows more streaks of interventionism than many in his political party and even many of his colleagues.
sentences.zh: 我想说，相比他所在的政党中的许多人甚至他的许多同僚，布林肯表现出更多干涉主义的倾向。

sentences.en: But you can see this really comes from his heart.
sentences.zh: 但你可以看出这确实发自他的内心。

sentences.en: No, no, Grover, it's not the unbuilding.
sentences.zh: 不，不，格罗弗，不是联合大厦（unbuilding）。

sentences.en: It's the U.N.
sentences.zh: 是联合国大厦（U.N. building）。

sentences.en: building.
sentences.zh: 大厦。

sentences.en: You hear it when he talks about why the United States needs to care about refugees.
sentences.zh: 当他谈到为什么美国需要关心难民时，你能听出来。

sentences.en: And one of the issues we're going to talk about is something really important.
sentences.zh: 我们要谈论的问题之一是一个非常重要的问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Refugees.
sentences.zh: 难民。

sentences.en: He even had a moment where he was explaining that to Grover on Sesame Street.
sentences.zh: 他甚至有过向《芝麻街》的格罗弗解释这一点的时刻。

sentences.en: These are people who've had to leave their homes because life in their countries was not safe for them.
sentences.zh: 这些人不得不离开家园，因为他们国家的的生活对他们而言不再安全。

sentences.en: Grover, can you imagine how difficult it would be to have to leave your home?
sentences.zh: 格罗弗，你能想象不得不离开家园会有多困难吗？

sentences.en: No, I cannot.
sentences.zh: 不，我无法想象。

sentences.en: I would never want to leave Sesame Street.
sentences.zh: 我永远不想离开芝麻街。

sentences.en: I cannot imagine leaving my apartment or my pet turtle Rufus behind.
sentences.zh: 我无法想象离开我的公寓或留下我的宠物乌龟鲁弗斯。

sentences.en: And so eventually, of course, Blinken links up with Joe Biden.
sentences.zh: 所以最终，毫无疑问，布林肯与乔·拜登走到了一起。

sentences.en: When is that and what are the circumstances?
sentences.zh: 那是什么时候，情况又是怎样的？

sentences.en: Well, about 20 years ago, he ends up on Biden's foreign relations staff and quickly becomes Biden's sort of chief national security advisor.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大约20年前，他进入了拜登的外交关系幕僚团队，并很快成为拜登的首席国家安全顾问。

sentences.en: And Biden, you have to remember, spent 17 years either as the chairman or the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee,
sentences.zh: 而且你必须记住，拜登有17年的时间要么担任参议院外交关系委员会的主席，要么担任资深成员，

sentences.en: flying around the world, meeting world leaders, convincing himself that much of diplomacy is all about personal relationships.
sentences.zh: 他飞往世界各地，会见世界领导人，并确信很大一部分外交工作全在于个人关系。

sentences.en: And when you look at the photos of those meetings, it was always Blinken who was standing just off to the side there as Biden's strategiSt.
sentences.zh: 当你看着那些会面的照片时，总是布林肯作为拜登的战略家站在一旁。

sentences.en: And how do Blinken's views, his inclination towards intervention, how does that line up with Biden's during this period when they're working together?
sentences.zh: 那么布林肯的观点、他对干预的倾向，在他们共事的这段时期里是如何与拜登的观点保持一致的？

sentences.en: Well, this is one of the more curious things about the relationship between Blinken and Biden, because it's very close.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这是布林肯和拜登之间关系中最奇妙的事情之一，因为他们关系非常亲密。

sentences.en: Biden deeply respects Blinken's views.
sentences.zh: 拜登非常尊重布林肯的观点。

sentences.en: He's the first one he goes and turns to for his opinion on these things.
sentences.zh: 他是拜登在这些事情上首先寻求意见的人。

sentences.en: But frequently, their instincts are different.
sentences.zh: 但通常，他们的直觉有所不同。

sentences.en: Let me give you a few examples.
sentences.zh: 我给你举几个例子。

sentences.en: When Biden becomes vice president and Blinken is his national security advisor, the first issue they had to go tackle in the Obama administration was, should the U.S.
sentences.zh: 当拜登成为副总统、布林肯担任他的国家安全顾问时，他们在奥巴马政府中需要解决的第一个问题是：美国应该

sentences.en: pull its forces out of Afghanistan?
sentences.zh: 从阿富汗撤军吗？

sentences.en: And while the commander in Afghanistan was calling for a force of over 100,000 and Hillary Clinton was debating about 50 or 60,000,
sentences.zh: 正当阿富汗的指挥官呼吁部署超过10万人的兵力、希拉里·克林顿讨论5万或6万人时，

sentences.en: Biden was taking the view that, no, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 拜登的观点是，不，美国应该

sentences.en: should be down to just a very small crew of counterterrorism operators, that we couldn't get anything done there.
sentences.zh: 只保留一小撮反恐作战人员，我们在那里无法完成任何任务。

sentences.en: And Blinken actually sort of more sided with the Hillary view of the world.
sentences.zh: 而布林肯实际上更倾向于希拉里的世界观。

sentences.en: What's interesting is that that view won the immediate day and Obama ended up doing a surge of forces.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，那种观点在当时占了上风，奥巴马最终决定增兵。

sentences.en: But Biden, in the end, kind of won the war, because now everyone from Donald Trump to Joe Biden is of the view that the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但拜登最终可以说是赢得了这场战争，因为现在从唐纳德·特朗普到乔·拜登，所有人都认为美国

sentences.en: should keep a pretty minimal force in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 应该在阿富汗保持相当少量的兵力。

sentences.en: That's what Trump did.
sentences.zh: 特朗普就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And I suspect that's what you'll see Biden do as well.
sentences.zh: 我猜你也会看到拜登这样做。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But importantly, in that story you just told, Blinken was not on the same page as Biden,
sentences.zh: 但重要的是，在你刚刚讲的那个故事中，布林肯和拜登并不在同一个频道上，

sentences.en: and it seems found a way to vocalize that he was pushing for a greater level of troops in Afghanistan.
sentences.zh: 而且他似乎找到了表达自己立场的方式，即在阿富汗推动更大规模的军力部署。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, it happened a second time then on the question of whether the United States should intervene in Libya to drive out Colonel Marmar Gaddafi.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，当美国是否应该干预利比亚以驱逐卡扎菲上校的问题出现时，这种情况发生了第二次。

sentences.en: This was at a moment when there was an uprising in Libya.
sentences.zh: 正值利比亚发生起义的时候。

sentences.en: Gaddafi was on the run.
sentences.zh: 卡扎菲在逃。

sentences.en: The Europeans wanted to go in and help the rebels by bombing them.
sentences.zh: 欧洲人想要介入并通过轰炸来帮助叛军。

sentences.en: Obama was very cautious.
sentences.zh: 奥巴马非常谨慎。

sentences.en: Clinton wanted to go join the Europeans in this effort.
sentences.zh: 克林顿希望加入欧洲人这一努力。

sentences.en: Joe Biden thought that this was a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 乔·拜登认为这是个坏主意。

sentences.en: Blinken thought it was a good idea.
sentences.zh: 布林顿则认为是个好主意。

sentences.en: And, of course, in the end, Gaddafi was driven from power.
sentences.zh: 当然，最后卡扎菲被赶下台。

sentences.en: He was on the run for months.
sentences.zh: 他逃亡了几个月。

sentences.en: Eventually, some local rebels pulled him out of a ditch and shot him.
sentences.zh: 最终，一些当地叛军把他从水沟里拖出来并枪决了。

sentences.en: But you could also argue that Biden's caution was understandable because Libya has been a mess ever since.
sentences.zh: 但你也可以认为拜登的谨慎是可以理解的，因为利比亚自那以后一直是一团糟。

sentences.en: But here again, Blinken disagrees with Biden.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，布林肯再次与拜登意见不一。

sentences.en: But this time, Blinken's view does win out in Libya.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，布林肯的观点在利比亚占了上风。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And a dictator was ousted, although I wouldn't say that the United States or anyone else had a strategic plan for what they would go do with Libya thereafter.
sentences.zh: 一个独裁者被赶下台，尽管我不会说美国或其他任何人在利比亚此后的走向上有过什么战略规划。

sentences.en: And, of course, it's been a pretty messy story ever since.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，从那以后那里的局势一直非常混乱。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the lesson here is pretty complicated.
sentences.zh: 所以这里的教训非常复杂。

sentences.en: Blinken and Biden seem to disagree a lot.
sentences.zh: 布林肯和拜登似乎经常意见不合。

sentences.en: And Biden's restraint has, in many cases, been proven prescient.
sentences.zh: 而且在很多情况下，事实证明拜登的克制是具有先见之明的。

sentences.en: Proven prescient from an American view of vital interests, right?
sentences.zh: 从美国核心利益的角度来看，事实证明这是有先见之明的，对吧？

sentences.en: Because this gets to the core question that Blinken's whole career kind of raises, which is humanitarian interventions are frequently important and critical to American values.
sentences.zh: 因为这触及了布林肯整个职业生涯所引发的核心问题，那就是人道主义干预往往非常重要，对美国的价值观至关重要。

sentences.en: But they're not defending vital American interests because you're going in and intervening in places where the conflict really has very little to do with the safety of the United States or the safety of Americans.
sentences.zh: 但它们并不是在捍卫美国的重大利益，因为你们介入并干预的那些地方，冲突其实与美国的安全或美国人民的安全关系不大。

sentences.en: David, of course, by the time Barack Obama leaves office and Anthony Blinken is no longer at the State Department,
sentences.zh: 大卫，当然，到了贝拉克·奥巴马卸任、安东尼·布林肯离开国务院的时候，

sentences.en: we now know that Americans and America had become deeply fatigued by all manner of U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们现在知道，美国人和美国已经对各种形式的美国

sentences.en: entanglements overseas.
sentences.zh: 海外纠葛感到深深的疲惫。

sentences.en: And we know that because Donald Trump is elected on this message of America first, on this message that America should get out of the world.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为唐纳德·特朗普正是凭借“美国优先”这一口号、凭借美国应该从世界抽身这一主张而当选的。

sentences.en: And that very much felt, I have to imagine, like a rejection of Blinkenism, of this interventionist approach.
sentences.zh: 我想，这在很大程度上让人感觉是对布林肯主义、对这种干预主义的一种否定。

sentences.en: And so I wonder how Blinken responded to that.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇布林肯对此作何反应。

sentences.en: He didn't respond well.
sentences.zh: 他的反应并不好。

sentences.en: He thinks that Donald Trump squandered the most valuable part of American power, which is the power of the American example.
sentences.zh: 他认为唐纳德·特朗普挥霍了美国力量中最宝贵的部分，那就是美国表率的力量。

sentences.en: There's a general sense that we've lost our North Star.
sentences.zh: 人们普遍感觉到我们失去了北极星。

sentences.en: People are increasingly confused.
sentences.zh: 人们越来越感到困惑。

sentences.en: They feel a sense of chaos.
sentences.zh: 他们感到了混乱。

sentences.en: They don't know which end is up.
sentences.zh: 他们分不清方向。

sentences.en: Whether we like it or not, the world tends not to organize itself.
sentences.zh: 不管我们喜欢与否，这个世界往往不会自我组织。

sentences.en: And what that means is that it's the United States that's going to have to step in to play that role.
sentences.zh: 这意味着必须由美国站出来扮演这个角色。

sentences.en: If we're not doing a lot of that organizing in terms of shaping the rules and the norms and the institutions through which countries relate to one or other, then one of two things.
sentences.zh: 如果我们不在塑造国家间交往的规则、规范和机构方面发挥很多组织作用，那么就会出现两种情况之一。

sentences.en: Either someone else is doing it and probably not in a way that advances our own interests and values.
sentences.zh: 要么是别人在做这件事，而且很可能不是以促进我们自身利益和价值观的方式。

sentences.en: Or maybe just as bad.
sentences.zh: 或者可能同样糟糕的是。

sentences.en: No one is.
sentences.zh: 根本没人做。

sentences.en: Because if we're not, it's not like no one else is going to play that role.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我们不做，并不是说没有其他人会扮演这个角色。

sentences.en: Vacuums will be created.
sentences.zh: 权力真空将会产生。

sentences.en: And then you tend to have chaos and a vacuum that may be filled by bad things before it's filled by good things.
sentences.zh: 然后你往往会面临混乱和一个可能在好事到来之前被坏事填满的真空。

sentences.en: He believes that Trump failed time and time again to do that.
sentences.zh: 他认为特朗普一次又一次地未能做到这一点。

sentences.en: It failed at NATO.
sentences.zh: 北约失败了。

sentences.en: It failed in East Asia.
sentences.zh: 东亚失败了。

sentences.en: It failed in putting together a common response to China.
sentences.zh: 在针对中国达成共同应对方面失败了。

sentences.en: And yet he recognizes half of America believes that Trump was essentially right here, that we're overextended, and that when we get out into the rest of the world,
sentences.zh: 然而他承认，半数美国人认为特朗普在这里基本上是对的，我们过度延伸了，当我们走出去接触世界的其他地方时，

sentences.en: we get taken to the cleaners.
sentences.zh: 我们被狠狠地敲诈了。

sentences.en: So the tension in the next few years is to see whether Blinken has the skills at home and abroad to make his case,
sentences.zh: 因此，未来几年的张力在于看看布林肯是否具备在国内外的技能来阐明他的观点，

sentences.en: to convince Americans that involvement in the world is in its interest, and to convince the world that America is back, and that once again,
sentences.zh: 说服美国人参与世界事务符合其利益，并说服世界美国回来了，并且又一次，

sentences.en: it will be the organizing center of global diplomacy.
sentences.zh: 它将成为全球外交的组织中心。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So, David, let's presume Anthony Blinken turns out to be a relatively skilled diplomatic salesman.
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，我们假设安东尼·布林肯原来是个相对娴熟的外交推销员。

sentences.en: What do you think his version of American foreign policy will actually look like in practice, given where everything now stands in America's relations with the rest of the world?
sentences.zh: 鉴于目前美国与世界其他关系现状，你认为他版本的美国外交政策在实践中究竟会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Well, with the allies, Michael, I think the early days will be pretty much a welcome back home festival, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，迈克尔，对于盟友来说，我认为早期基本上就是一个“欢迎回家”的节日，对吧？

sentences.en: Because they're going to spend the first few months rejoining the world or rejoining agreements that Donald Trump walked away from.
sentences.zh: 因为他们将花前几个月重新加入世界，或重新加入唐纳德·特朗普退出的协议。

sentences.en: They're going to re-sign the Paris Accord on climate change in the early days.
sentences.zh: 他们将在早期重新签署关于气候变化的《巴黎协定》。

sentences.en: They're going to re-join the World Health Organization, which President Trump walked out of in the middle of COVID, arguing that the Chinese had too much influence while the U.S.
sentences.zh: 他们将重新加入世界卫生组织，特朗普总统在疫情期间退出了该组织，理由是美国

sentences.en: paid the bills.
sentences.zh: 付钱的同时中国人拥有太多影响力。

sentences.en: They're going to go announce a re-commitment to NATO.
sentences.zh: 他们将宣布重新致力于北约。

sentences.en: So they're going to do a lot of dismantling of the dismantling.
sentences.zh: 所以他们将对过去的拆解进行大量的撤销工作。

sentences.en: You know, among Blinken's friends, they call it the great undoing, right?
sentences.zh: 你知道，在布林肯的朋友们看来，这被称为“伟大的倒回”，对吧？

sentences.en: That they're trying to go undo the Trump era.
sentences.zh: 他们试图去撤销特朗普时代。

sentences.en: But, of course, a couple things are going to get in the way.
sentences.zh: 但是，当然，会有一些事情挡路。

sentences.en: The biggest example of this may be Iran.
sentences.zh: 这方面最大的例子可能是伊朗。

sentences.en: Right, where we know that President-elect Joe Biden wants to return to a pre-Trump diplomatic relationship and specifically wants to rejoin the Iran nuclear deal.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们知道当选总统乔·拜登希望回到特朗普之前的外交关系，特别是希望重新加入伊朗核协议。

sentences.en: Well, that's right, but because of what President Trump has done over the past two years,
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实如此，但由于特朗普总统在过去两年中所做的一切，

sentences.en: and because of what the Israelis are believed to have been responsible for in the past few days, that's going to be a really, really tall order.
sentences.zh: 以及据信以色列人在过去几天里所做的事情，这将是一项非常非常艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: David, explain that.
sentences.zh: 大卫，解释一下这一点。

sentences.en: Well, over the past few years, President Trump has done everything he could to unwind and complicate the Obama-era Iran nuclear accord.
sentences.zh: 嗯，在过去的几年里，特朗普总统竭尽全力瓦解和使奥巴马时代的伊核协议变得复杂。

sentences.en: And in the past few days, the Israelis have tried to put the final nail in the coffin of that agreement.
sentences.zh: 而在过去几天里，以色列人试图给该协议钉上最后一颗棺材钉。

sentences.en: Tonight, Iran says its most senior nuclear scientist has been assassinated near the capital, Tehran.
sentences.zh: 今晚，伊朗称其最高核科学家在首都德黑兰附近被暗杀。

sentences.en: With this assassination on the streets of a little town outside of Tehran last Friday.
sentences.zh: 在上周五德黑兰郊外小镇的街道上发生这起暗杀事件时。

sentences.en: He was a protected and prized scientiSt.
sentences.zh: 他是一位受到保护和珍视的科学家。

sentences.en: We're the leading Iranian nuclear scientist driving to his summer place.
sentences.zh: 我们是这位开着车前往避暑别墅的伊朗顶尖核科学家。

sentences.en: Iranian officials say Mohsen Fakhrizadeh was ambushed in his car by what they call armed terrorists, spraying the windshield with bullets.
sentences.zh: 伊朗官员称，穆赫辛·法克里扎德的车遭到他们所谓的武装恐怖分子的伏击，风挡玻璃被子弹扫射。

sentences.en: He's intercepted by a group of assassins and killed in broad daylight.
sentences.zh: 他遭到一群刺客的拦截，并在光天化日之下被杀害。

sentences.en: Iran's President Hassan Rouhani blamed Israel for the killing on Saturday.
sentences.zh: 伊朗总统哈桑·鲁哈尼周六将这起谋杀归咎于以色列。

sentences.en: There's a lot of evidence that this was done by the Israelis.
sentences.zh: 有大量证据表明这是以色列人干的。

sentences.en: Iran is already vowing revenge.
sentences.zh: 伊朗已经誓言要进行报复。

sentences.en: And a fair bit of speculation that the Israelis wouldn't have done it without first giving warning to the United States.
sentences.zh: 而且有相当多的猜测认为，以色列人若不先警告美国，是不会动手的。

sentences.en: We don't know that yet.
sentences.zh: 我们目前还不知道这一点。

sentences.en: This is now making it extremely difficult for Iran to come back to the table and for Biden to re-execute a workable strategy for Iran.
sentences.zh: 这现在使得伊朗极难重返谈判桌，也让拜登极难重新实施对伊朗可行的战略。

sentences.en: But what we do know is that the result is that the assassination took what was already an incredibly difficult diplomatic challenge, reassembling the nuclear deal,
sentences.zh: 但我们所知道的是，暗杀的结果让本已极其困难的外交挑战——重新拼凑伊核协议——

sentences.en: and made it vastly harder.
sentences.zh: 变得难上加难。

sentences.en: Because now Blinken and Biden walk into a world in which the Iranians are understandably hopping mad and will believe themselves that the Americans were in on it.
sentences.zh: 因为现在布林肯和拜登进入这样一个世界：伊朗人气得发疯，而且他们自己会相信美国人也参与其中。

sentences.en: And the hardliners will say, see, you never should have entered that deal to begin with.
sentences.zh: 强硬派会说：看吧，你们一开始就根本不该签署那个协议。

sentences.en: So this is a very clear example of how the Trump foreign policy approach may actually make it all but impossible for the Biden-Blinken foreign policy approach to actually work.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常清晰的例子，说明特朗普的外交政策方针实际上可能让拜登-布林肯的外交政策方针几乎无法真正发挥作用。

sentences.en: Because if the Iranians say, hey, you've trashed this deal and you have taken out our top nuclear scientists, why on earth would we rejoin an agreement with your country?
sentences.zh: 因为如果伊朗人说，嘿，你们毁了这个协议，还干掉了我们顶尖的核科学家，我们凭什么要重新加入与你们国家的协议？

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Iranians are going to take that view.
sentences.zh: 伊朗人会持这种观点。

sentences.en: But it gets even more complicated than that.
sentences.zh: 但事情比这还要复杂。

sentences.en: Because while there are a lot of people who would say, let's just rewind the clock to January 20th, 2017, when Barack Obama left office, the fact is the world's moved on, right?
sentences.zh: 因为尽管有很多人会说，让我们把时钟拨回2017年1月20日贝拉克·奥巴马卸任的时候，但事实是世界已经前进了，对吧？

sentences.en: The Iran situation is far more complicated than it was in 2017.
sentences.zh: 伊朗局势比2017年要复杂得多。

sentences.en: And that's not the only place around the world where it's more complicated.
sentences.zh: 而且这并不是世界上唯一一个变得更加复杂的地方。

sentences.en: The North Koreans, for all those love letters that they wrote to President Trump, have built a lot more fuel for nuclear weapons.
sentences.zh: 朝鲜人写给特朗普总统的所有那些情书并没有阻止他们为核武器制造更多燃料。

sentences.en: The Chinese have expanded their footprint in the South China Sea and become much more aggressive in their technology exports.
sentences.zh: 中国人在南海扩大了足迹，在技术出口方面变得更加具有攻击性。

sentences.en: All around the world,
sentences.zh: 在世界各地，

sentences.en: you're finding places where issues that Biden and Blinken were familiar with and thought they might have a handle on when they were leaving office have now come back with a vengeance.
sentences.zh: 你会发现一些地方，拜登和布林肯曾经熟悉并在卸任时以为自己能掌控的议题现在卷土重来。

sentences.en: And it will not be easy for the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国想要像钥匙插进点火开关那样

sentences.en: to just insert itself back like a key in ignition.
sentences.zh: 轻而易举地重新插入并不容易。

sentences.en: That's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So now Blinken comes in with his view that America must be the organizing force.
sentences.zh: 所以现在布林肯带着他的观点上台，即美国必须成为组织力量。

sentences.en: But, you know, in all those cases, Michael, it's not clear that the world is particularly interested in seeing the United States come back in as an organizing force.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，在所有这些情况下，迈克尔，世界是否特别有兴趣看到美国重新作为一个组织力量回来，这一点并不明确。

sentences.en: Because there's a fundamental question that Blinken and Biden are going to have to face, which is that the world's going to say to them, why should we trust you?
sentences.zh: 因为布林肯和拜登将面临一个根本性的问题，即世界会对他们说：我们凭什么信任你们？

sentences.en: Sure, we're glad to see an engaged America come back and we're delighted you're coming back into all these treaties.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们很高兴看到一个积极参与的世界重新回来，我们也很高兴你们重新加入所有这些条约。

sentences.en: But supposing this is just a four-year blip and that when we look back at it,
sentences.zh: 但假设这只是四年的一个小插曲，当我们回首往事时，

sentences.en: Trumpism ultimately is going to rule the day and that the next president's going to go undo whatever you go do in the next four years.
sentences.zh: 特朗普主义最终将占上风，下一任总统会去撤销你们在未来四年里所做的一切呢？

sentences.en: So Biden and Blinken have to not only convince the world that America is back and not only convince them that they should trust us as an organizing force,
sentences.zh: 所以拜登和布林肯不仅要让世界相信美国回来了，不仅要让他们相信他们应该信任我们作为一种组织力量，

sentences.en: but they also have to convince them that the whole concept that we call liberal internationalism,
sentences.zh: 而且他们还必须让他们相信我们称之为自由国际主义的整个概念，

sentences.en: that the United States brings its values with it around the world and will back those up with force or with money or with influence,
sentences.zh: 即美国将把其价值观带到世界各地，并用武力、金钱或影响力来支持这些价值观，

sentences.en: that that's a view that's actually going to stick.
sentences.zh: 这种观点实际上是会坚持下去的。

sentences.en: You know, Blinken has this phrase that he's used many times, which is superpowers don't bluff.
sentences.zh: 你知道，布林肯多次使用过这样一句话：超级大国从不虚张声势。

sentences.en: And the trick for him and for President Biden over the next few years is going to be convincing them that in saying we're back, we're not bluffing.
sentences.zh: 他和拜登总统在未来几年里的诀窍将是说服他们：当我们在说我们回来时，我们不是在虚张声势。

sentences.en: So, David, the challenge for Anthony Blinken, if he is confirmed as our new secretary of state, will not just be, as you said earlier,
sentences.zh: 所以，大卫，如果安东尼·布林肯被确认为我们的新国务卿，他所面临的挑战将不仅仅如你刚才所说，

sentences.en: selling a skeptical United States electorate on this approach to foreign policy,
sentences.zh: 向一个持怀疑态度的美国选民群体兜售这种外交政策方法，

sentences.en: which is in and of itself a pretty tall order, it's actually selling a deeply skeptical world that this can be counted on for more than just a few years.
sentences.zh: 这本身就是一项相当艰巨的任务，而是要向一个深表怀疑的世界兜售这种方法，让人相信它不仅能维持几年。

sentences.en: That's exactly right, Michael.
sentences.zh: 完全正确，迈克尔。

sentences.en: He's got to go convince Americans that a re-engaged America is truly in Americans' own interest and in the interest of American workers.
sentences.zh: 他必须让美国人相信，一个重新参与的美国真正符合美国人自身的利益和美国工人的利益。

sentences.en: And he's got to convince our allies that we are actually there to stay, that Trump and Trumpism isn't coming back.
sentences.zh: 他必须让我们的盟友相信我们确实会留下来，特朗普和特朗普主义不会卷土重来。

sentences.en: And those are tall orders, both at home and abroad.
sentences.zh: 无论在国内还是国外，这些都是艰巨的任务。

sentences.en: Well, David, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，大卫，非常感谢。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们不胜感激。

sentences.en: Michael, great to be with you.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，很高兴能和你在一起。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Trump reportedly spoke with Giuliani about a pardon for him.
sentences.zh: 据报道，特朗普曾与朱利安尼谈过关于赦免他的事。

sentences.en: As recently as last week, Giuliani has been under investigation by federal prosecutors in Manhattan for his business dealings in Ukraine
sentences.zh: 就在上周，朱利安尼因其在乌克兰的商业交易

sentences.en: and for his role in ousting the American ambassador there, a plot at the heart of Trump's impeachment.
sentences.zh: 以及他在驱逐美国驻乌克兰大使（特朗普弹劾案核心的一场阴谋）中的角色，一直在接受曼哈顿联邦检察官的调查。

sentences.en: And in an interview on Tuesday, Attorney General Bill Barr said there was no evidence of voter fraud
sentences.zh: 并且在周二的一次采访中，司法部长比尔·巴尔表示，没有证据表明存在足以改变选举结果的选民欺诈，

sentences.en: that could alter the outcome of the election, directly undercutting claims by President Trump.
sentences.zh: 这直接削弱了特朗普总统的说法。

sentences.en: Barr's comments to the Associated Press made him the most high-profile member of the president's cabinet to affirm Joe Biden's victory.
sentences.zh: 巴尔对美联社的评论使他成为总统内阁中最高调确认乔·拜登胜利的成员。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了群自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就一直陷入一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人兴奋的斗争之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《都市》中，我和萨拉·科尼格将带你了解那些试图保持影响力却在途中失去控制的人的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在您获取播客的任何地方收听。
